sequencing_note: User asked directly for two things together: wire the grant to a first real route (auth/password) and build the rest of plan #17 (enroll/cert-rotation/factory-reset). This evidence file covers everything EXCEPT certificate rotation -- recon into what 'bounded local listener/handshake verification' and the 'retain the previous confirmed slot through one successful reboot' rollback protocol (plan #12) actually require found a genuinely large, novel piece of work (new mbedtls CLIENT-side TLS code this project has never written, a new persisted multi-boot activation/rollback state machine analogous to but separate from the existing OTA rollback mechanism, a new temporary local listener instance) -- comparable in size to everything else built in this whole session combined, and realistically needing real hardware HIL verification (the self-test and reboot-rollback protocol are not meaningfully host-testable). Flagging this rather than attempting it blind, matching this session's own established pattern of pausing on newly-discovered large scope.

design_decisions.decision: PhysicalPresenceActionClass gained two members beyond plan #20's own seven (kProvisioningEnroll, kAdminPasswordChange) -- already covered by the physical-presence-grant sub-slice's own evidence file, exercised for real here for the first time.
design_decisions.why: See that sub-slice's own documented rationale; this sub-slice is the first real consumer of both new values.

design_decisions.decision: The provisioning secret (manufacturing/development proof-of-possession, S6 'Provisioning and credentials' #2) is now fetched exactly ONCE, in WebServer::start(), and cached for the listener's whole lifetime -- not re-fetched per request.
design_decisions.why: provisioning_secret_provider_get()'s own documented development-mode behavior draws FRESH randomness on every call (never persisted). Calling it per-request would make a real challenge/response impossible in development mode: the value an installer reads from the boot-time log would never match what a later request-time fetch generates. Caching once is what makes 'installer reads the logged value, then submits it back' work at all -- a real, load-bearing fix, not a caching optimization. Production's value is deterministic either way, so caching changes nothing there.

design_decisions.decision: auth/password verifies the CURRENT credential BEFORE consuming the physical-presence grant.
design_decisions.why: A wrong-password attempt must not burn a real installer's one-time, 60-second grant -- ordering the checks this way means only a genuinely correct request can ever consume it.

design_decisions.decision: provisioning/enroll and login are both registered UNWRAPPED (not through register_authenticated_uri_handler_v1()).
design_decisions.why: Both are reached without an existing session -- enroll is what CREATES the first admin credential at all. Wrapping either would make the route require already being logged in, which is circular.

design_decisions.decision: gateway-identity manufacturing-record verification (Section 2.9, FD-17) is checked in enroll only under CONFIG_ZGW_PRODUCTION_PROFILE, skipped entirely in development.
design_decisions.why: No manufacturing record is ever populated in development either, and development already carries weaker trust guarantees throughout this codebase (Section 2.7's own plain-HTTP posture) -- gating development enrollment on a check that can only ever fail there would make development enrollment permanently impossible, serving no real security purpose in a profile that already trusts less.

design_decisions.decision: factory-reset/operations validates PoP and consumes the physical-presence grant for REAL (not a no-op), only returning capability_unavailable (503) once both checks pass.
design_decisions.why: Plan #22's own text: 'S6 owns policy validation; S8 owns the reset journal and erase execution.' Read literally, the POLICY half is real work for S6 to do, not deferred -- only the actual erase execution is S8's job. A stub that always returns 503 regardless of policy checks would silently skip #22 entirely rather than partially implementing it as the plan's own stage split describes.

design_decisions.decision: New ApiV1ErrorCode::kPhysicalPresenceRequired (403) and kProvisioningNotActive (409), rather than reusing kCsrfOrOriginInvalid/kCapabilityUnavailable.
design_decisions.why: Distinct real conditions deserve distinct stable tokens under plan #23's 'non-leaky stable errors' -- reusing an existing code with a different real meaning would itself be a small leak (a client could no longer tell 'wrong CSRF' from 'no physical presence' by token, weakening the API's own stated contract that every failure resolves to exactly one meaning).

real_defects_found_and_fixed_this_sub_sl.defect: New auth/password and factory-reset test scenarios segfaulted / gave wrong results.
real_defects_found_and_fixed_this_sub_sl.root_cause: Three separate, real test-authoring bugs, all found via a debug-then-ASan-then-manual-trace process, none in production code: (1) reusing the same httpd_req_t across multiple calls through a WRAPPED route without resetting req.user_ctx to the wrapper's own captured binding before each call -- the trampoline overwrites req.user_ctx with the real WebRouteContext* on every ALLOWED pass regardless of what the real handler decides afterward, so a second call reusing the same (now-polluted) req.user_ctx misinterprets a WebRouteContext* as an AuthenticatedRouteBinding*; (2) creating physical-presence grants/commissioning windows with an arbitrary fixed timestamp (1000ULL) instead of hal_time_now_ms() -- the real handler code checks elapsed time against the SAME real monotonic clock, so a mismatched basis made every grant look either already-expired or created-in-the-future; (3) the test's own httpd_req_recv mock destructively drains g_request_body as it is read, so reusing a stale g_request_body across a second handler call (only updating content_len from its now-empty size) fed an effectively-empty body to the second read_request_body() call.
real_defects_found_and_fixed_this_sub_sl.fix: All three fixed directly in the test file (reset req.user_ctx before every wrapped-route call reusing the same req object; use hal_time_now_ms() for every grant/window creation the test performs; reassign g_request_body immediately before every handler call that will read a body). Verified via a full ASan+UBSan rebuild after each fix, then the full host suite.

honest_scope_boundary: Nothing in this repository yet turns a real button press into a physical-presence grant (no debounce/edge-detection task exists) -- every route built this round that consumes a grant will always return 403 physical_presence_required against a real client today. This is the same honest, deliberate gap the physical-presence-grant sub-slice's own evidence already names, now exercised by three more real call sites.

provisioning/enroll's development-mode PoP flow depends on an installer actually reading the boot-time serial log for the cached secret -- untested against a real installer workflow, only against the mechanism's own correctness (the cached value matches what gets logged, and matches what a later request must submit).

Certificate rotation (plan #12, POST /api/v1/security/certificates/operations) is explicitly NOT part of this sub-slice -- see this file's own sequencing_note for the real complexity recon that led to flagging it as its own separate piece of work rather than attempting it now.
